content.value_statement: Type gaps can break full-stack TypeScript applications at runtime. This skill shows validation and API patterns that keep data typed from database to UI.
actual_capabilities: Explains Zod schemas, inferred types, transforms, refinements, discriminated unions, and recursive types.
Shows tRPC server procedures and typed client calls with Zod inputs.
Demonstrates Prisma models, typed queries, nested creates, and relation includes.
Covers TypeScript features such as satisfies, decorators, const tuples, and strict compiler options.
Provides full-stack Next.js examples for typed API handlers and React queries.
limitations: Does not run type checkers or install packages by itself.
Examples are illustrative and require adaptation for each project.
Does not replace security review for authorization, authentication, or data exposure.
Requires TypeScript, Zod, tRPC, and Prisma knowledge for advanced usage.

use_cases.title: Design Typed API Inputs
use_cases.description: Create validation boundaries for request data before it reaches business logic.

use_cases.title: Connect Database and UI Types
use_cases.description: Align Prisma models, tRPC routers, and React query usage in one typed flow.

use_cases.title: Plan TypeScript Migrations
use_cases.description: Identify strict compiler settings and validation patterns for safer migration work.

prompt_templates.title: Validate an API Input
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this API input shape and suggest a Zod validation schema, inferred TypeScript type, and clear validation errors.

prompt_templates.title: Add Runtime Validation
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the data boundaries in this feature and explain where runtime validation should happen with Zod.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Typed tRPC Router
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a tRPC router for these operations with Zod inputs, typed outputs, and Prisma access patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Full-Stack Type Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert request for an end-to-end review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this full-stack feature for type gaps from database model to client UI, then list fixes by risk and effort.

output_examples.input: Review a user creation endpoint that accepts email, name, role, and optional metadata.
output_examples.output: The review recommends validation for email format, allowed role values, metadata shape, and user-facing error messages.

output_examples.input: Plan a tRPC posts feature backed by Prisma and displayed in React.
output_examples.output: The plan defines validated list and create operations, typed database queries, pagination boundaries, and client query states.

output_examples.input: Audit a TypeScript migration that still uses loose any types.
output_examples.output: The audit prioritizes strict compiler settings, unknown for external data, type guards, and validation at API boundaries.

best_practices: Validate untrusted data at API, form, environment, and external service boundaries.
Infer TypeScript types from validation schemas to avoid duplicate model definitions.
Keep database, API, and UI contracts aligned through typed routers and strict compiler settings.
anti_patterns: Trusting client input because TypeScript types compile successfully.
Duplicating validation schemas and TypeScript interfaces by hand.
Using broad any types across database, API, and UI boundaries.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps build TypeScript applications with validated inputs, typed APIs, and database-aware type flow.

faq.question: Does it execute code or install dependencies?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples that users must adapt and run in their own projects.

faq.question: Which libraries does it focus on?
faq.answer: It focuses on Zod, tRPC, Prisma, React, Next.js, and modern TypeScript features.

faq.question: Can it replace manual API security review?
faq.answer: No. It improves validation and typing, but authorization and data exposure still need review.

faq.question: Is it useful for JavaScript migrations?
faq.answer: Yes. It suggests validation boundaries and strict typing patterns for migration work.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
